doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sixties: Verve end, California, Half Note, Duets
title: Living in California
summary: He moved to Carmel Valley with his wife, did odd jobs, and declined to sit in with Miles.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Let’s talk about that. What prompted that? When did you do it?

I was living in Lennie’s house with my then wife and she came from Alameda, California. Her parents were there and we just decided that it would be a good idea to get out of the situation and get a perspective on what was happening so we lived in Carmel Valley for a year and just enjoyed that environment. I didn’t play very much. At some point Lennie contacted me to play at the Half Note and I wasn’t really ready for that but I finally . . . I think I missed one flight because I didn’t want to go just in fear that I wasn’t up to it. Then I went and that was the last time we played together. Sixty-four that was.
Yeah. I want to talk about that in a minute because that was the . . . but just a little bit more about California. How were you making a living? Were you doing day gigs?

Some little painting [of] a bathroom, doing some garden work, things like that. I had an occasional teaching afternoon in San Jose sometimes. I would drive there and play some little gigs but nothing regular. Nothing terribly significant.

There was a thing in Ira Gitler’s book “Jazz Masters of the Forties” where he talks about [how] you told him there was a point where Miles was appearing with his band at the Blackhawk or something with Frank Strozier and Miles asked you to sit in. What happened there?
I just didn’t feel like doing that.
